title: 802.1X / EAP-TLS Authentication Flow
description: A sequence diagram of 802.1X port-based network access control using EAP-TLS, showing how a supplicant authenticates through an authenticator that only relays traffic to a RADIUS server, with the mutual TLS handshake highlighted.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity

educational.topic: Advanced Network Defense: Wireless, DNS, and Zero Trust
learningObjectives: Trace the 802.1X / EAP-TLS message flow from EAPOL-Start to an opened port.
Explain the distinct role of the supplicant, authenticator, and RADIUS server.
Explain why the authenticator can relay EAP without ever seeing the secrets.
educational.prerequisites: Familiarity with certificates, TLS handshakes, and basic LAN/Wi-Fi access.

pedagogical.interaction: Static, color-coded, responsive sequence diagram with the TLS handshake step highlighted.
pedagogical.assessment: Lesson plan asks students to identify which party validates the client certificate and why.
pedagogical.misconceptions: Counters the idea that the access point itself authenticates the user.

chapter_title: "Advanced Network Defense: Wireless, DNS, and Zero Trust"
